transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~90 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Sofia, Noah, Liam, Maya, Alex, Riley, Jordan
Notes: internal roadmap/launch readiness; recording via internal meet; slides referenced: Q4_launch_deck_v3 (drive link), postmortem: sept-release-rca.md

[00:00] Priya: ok everyone thanks for joining, tight agenda today, we've got 90 minutes, main focus is launch readiness for the runtime changes shipping in Q4. we'll start with the incident review from the sept release, then move into perf/latency concerns, observability gaps, and finish with rollout/canary plan. quick on who has any blockers?

[00:28] Ethan: yeah I'll flag right away the tail latency we saw on the 99th pctl, it spiked after we rolled the kernel patch, we saw some KV cache pressure, and also batching behavior changed for long seqs.

[00:45] Sofia: to add to that, the release had a mix of quantized and fp16 variants, and the scheduler favored packing that ended up creating higher memory churn on some nodes. that triggered retries and a couple of cascaded timeouts.

[01:12] Noah: observability note, our dashboards didn't surface the slow start behavior quickly enough. the per-route retention is short for high-resolution percentiles so by the time on-call triaged we only had aggregated 5m windows. 

[01:40] Priya: ok so incident summary: kernel patch + scheduling change + packing edge case + short retention on metrics. can we confirm that's the causal chain?

[01:55] Liam: yep that's the rough chain. the kernel change improved average throughput but under certain sequence length distribution it amplified KV cache eviction, which then pushed requests into longer tails. we missed it in staging because our load generator wasn't hitting the same seq length mix.

[02:20] Alex: quick question — was this the A/B canary we ran or a full rollout? I remember we had canary but the traffic ramping was a bit faster than planned.

[02:33] Sofia: that was a partial canary but the routing policy allowed spillover to general pool due to an autoscale event; so partial canary but with gaps.

[03:00] Priya: actionable then: tighten canary gating and make sure traffic doesn't bleed. Sofia can update the playbook. add auto-rollback thresholds so we don't have to manual intervene.

[03:22] Sofia: noted. I'll add explicit thresholds: 99th pctl > x ms for more than 5 minutes -> auto rollback. also add a preflight check for seq length distribution match.

[03:45] Ethan: about perf benchmarking — we need runs that include both 1024 and 2048 seq lengths, and include quantized and non-quantized. current bench is too biased to short seqs. I can take lead but need compute.

[04:10] Liam: i'll provision a small dedicated pool for canary/perf. thinking 2x A100 equiv should be enough to replicate behaviors without blowing budget. I'll validate network and k8s configs.

[04:35] Riley: QA note, we'll add regression tests for tail latency and run nightly; also we'll create synthetic traces to exercise the KV eviction path.

[04:55] Priya: perfect. Noah, on observability what are the quick wins?

[05:05] Noah: short list: increase retention for per-route high-res metrics to 14 days for p90/p99, add an anomaly detection alert on rising 99th pctl and on request retry rate. also expose KV cache hit/miss per node to dashboards.

[05:30] Maya: adding to that, we'll want to tag the metrics by deployment and canary cohort so we can slice quickly. current tagging is a bit coarse.

[05:48] Jordan: operations perspective — we need clear on-call playbook tweaks, and a dry-run of the incident response. can we schedule a DR drill next week?

[06:02] Priya: yes let's do a dry-run. Jordan and Riley own.

[06:15] --- Topic shift: Performance targets and cost tradeoffs ---

[06:20] Priya: for Q4 we have target latency SLOs: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 450ms for hosted medium tier. our cost goal is to reduce avg cost per token by 8% through batching and improved kernel selection. can we realistically hit both?

[06:40] Ethan: short answer: maybe. batching helps for throughput but hurts tail latency for small interactive requests. runtime improvements and smarter routing by request type can help. the new kernel selection helps avg but we saw tail regressions in the incident.

[07:05] Liam: we should consider request routing by priority: interactive vs batch. route interactive to low-batch mode nodes with reserved capacity. that costs more but preserves latency.

[07:25] Priya: is reserved capacity the Dedicated pool we offer or just an internal config?

[07:33] Liam: both — internally we can reserve a small pool for interactive, and the product can expose reserved pools. For this rollout let's do an internal reserved canary pool.

[07:45] Maya: reminder: we need to capture these config changes in the rollout deck and the ops runbook. I'll update the deck and link in the doc.

[08:05] --- Incident RCA details ---

[08:10] Sofia: the root cause itemization: 1) scheduler change packed incompatible seq lengths, 2) kernel change impacted cache eviction heuristics, 3) staging didn't mirror prod seq distribution, 4) metrics retention too short.

[08:40] Ethan: mitigation already in flight: revert kernel patch on nodes failing health checks; adjusted scheduling policy to avoid aggressive packing; limit canary ramp to 10% for next rollout.

[09:00] Priya: can we ensure this next rollout uses an updated load generator that mimics customer seq distribution? Alex can you coordinate with infra team on training load?

[09:12] Alex: yep will coordinate and pull samples from prod anonymized.

[09:25] --- Observability deep-dive ---

[09:30] Noah: showing the dashboard (referencing dash: q4-launch-observe.png), the problem area is the 99th pctl step change around 14:32 UTC on Sept 18. we lost granularity because rollup reduced resolution. Proposed: 14-day retention at 1s granularity for p90/p99 for top 20 routes.

[10:00] Priya: cost of retention?

[10:05] Noah: small but not trivial. we need to trade storage vs faster detection; I'd rather pay for early detection than a costly outage.

[10:18] Priya: agreed. add to roadmap as prioritized item.

[10:30] --- Rollout / Canary plan ---

[10:32] Sofia: proposed canary steps: deploy to canary pool (5% traffic) -> monitor 99th pctl and retry rate for 30 minutes -> if stable ramp to 25% for 1hr -> then 50% -> full. Auto-rollback if 99th pctl increases by >30% or retries > threshold.

[11:00] Ethan: we should instrument prefixed caching and KV cache metrics to evaluate real impact during canary. Also the perf bench should run on the canary pool in parallel to get numbers.

[11:25] Liam: I'll set up the dedicated pool and ensure routing rules. but we need to confirm infra quotas with finance. Priya, can you ok the small temporary quota?

[11:40] Priya: yes ok but keep it scoped and timeboxed. include cost estimates in the notes.

[11:52] --- Questions / Risks ---

[11:55] Riley: QA risk: flaky test coverage for long seqs; need to add synthetic scenarios.

[12:05] Jordan: operational risk: if auto-rollback triggers frequently we need to ensure we have a plan to revert config safely and notify customers. add escalation path.

[12:20] Priya: we'll add an escalation path in the playbook.

[12:35] --- Recap and next steps ---

[12:40] Priya: recap: Ethan run perf bench (1024/2048 + quant), Liam provision canary pool, Sofia update playbook with thresholds and preflight checks, Noah extend metric retention and add alerts, Riley add regression tests, Jordan schedule DR drill. owners and due dates assigned in action items. We'll reconvene next Tue for preliminary perf numbers. Any final comments?

[12:58] Ethan: small ask — include model variant matrix in the perf doc (fp16 vs int8) so we know which kernels to test.

[13:10] Maya: I'll circulate meeting notes, links to deck and postmortem, and create the follow-up calendar invite.

[13:20] Priya: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
